_comment: Raptor's egg library (library/README.md). Written from scratch.
name: MediaMTX
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: MediaMTX is a media server that takes live video and audio over RTSP, RTMP, SRT or WebRTC and serves it to viewers over all of them and HLS. The egg sets it up so anyone can watch, and only the publish user, with a password made at install, can send streams.

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# MediaMTX: downloads MediaMTX from its GitHub releases, checked against
# GitHub's checksum. mediamtx.yml is only written on the first install
# (with publishing locked behind a password); after that it's the owner's,
# and recordings are never touched. The binary is only replaced once the
# new one has downloaded and checked out.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server

repo=bluenviron/mediamtx
fail() { echo "$1"; exit 1; }
# gh_tag <latest|tag> prints the release's tag; returns 1 when there's no
# such release, 2 when GitHub can't be reached.
gh_tag() {
    local out
    out=$(gh-release tag "$repo" "$1" 2>&1) && { echo "$out"; return 0; }
    case "$out" in *"has no release"* | *"no releases"*) return 1 ;; *) return 2 ;; esac
}
offline="GitHub can't be reached right now, or is limiting downloads. Reinstall to try again in a few minutes."
case "$(uname -m)" in
    x86_64) arch=amd64 ;;
    aarch64) arch=arm64 ;;
    *) fail "MediaMTX has no build for this CPU ($(uname -m))." ;;
esac

version="${VERSION:-latest}"
case "$version" in latest|v*) ;; *) version="v$version" ;; esac
rc=0; tag=$(gh_tag "$version") || rc=$?
if [ "$rc" = 1 ]; then
    latest=$(gh_tag latest) || fail "$offline"
    fail "MediaMTX has no version ${VERSION}. Set Version to latest, or to a release such as ${latest#v}."
fi
[ "$rc" = 0 ] || fail "$offline"
version=$tag
asset="mediamtx_${version}_linux_${arch}.tar.gz"
assets=$(gh-release assets "$repo" "$version") || fail "$offline"
sum=$(awk -v a="$asset" '$1 == a { print $2 }' <<<"$assets")
[ -n "$sum" ] || fail "MediaMTX $version has no Linux build for this CPU. Choose another version."

tmp=/mnt/server/.raptor-build
rm -rf "$tmp" && mkdir -p "$tmp"
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
if [ -x mediamtx ] && [ "$(cat .raptor-mediamtx 2>/dev/null)" = "$sum" ]; then
    echo "MediaMTX $version is already installed."
else
    echo "Downloading MediaMTX $version"
    gh-release download "$repo" "$version" "$asset" "$tmp/mediamtx.tar.gz" || fail "The download failed or didn't match GitHub's checksum. Reinstall to try again."
    tar -xzf "$tmp/mediamtx.tar.gz" -C "$tmp" mediamtx mediamtx.yml
    mv -f "$tmp/mediamtx" mediamtx
    echo "$sum" > .raptor-mediamtx
fi

# The shipped config lets anyone publish a stream. On the first install,
# keep reading open (that's what a media server is for) but make publishing
# need the user "publish" with a random password, and use RTSP over TCP
# (RTP over UDP needs two more ports that the server doesn't have).
if [ ! -f mediamtx.yml ]; then
    if [ ! -f "$tmp/mediamtx.yml" ]; then
        gh-release download "$repo" "$version" "$asset" "$tmp/mediamtx.tar.gz" || fail "The download failed or didn't match GitHub's checksum. Reinstall to try again."
        tar -xzf "$tmp/mediamtx.tar.gz" -C "$tmp" mediamtx.yml
    fi
    password=$(head -c 18 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -d '/+=')
    awk -v pass="$password" '
        /^authInternalUsers:/ {
            print "authInternalUsers:"
            print "  # Anyone can watch and play recordings."
            print "  - user: any"
            print "    pass:"
            print "    ips: []"
            print "    permissions:"
            print "      - action: read"
            print "      - action: playback"
            print "  # Publishing needs this user and password."
            print "  - user: publish"
            print "    pass: " pass
            print "    ips: []"
            print "    permissions:"
            print "      - action: publish"
            print "  # The API, metrics and pprof, from the server itself only."
            print "  - user: any"
            print "    pass:"
            print "    ips: [\"127.0.0.1\", \"::1\"]"
            print "    permissions:"
            print "      - action: api"
            print "      - action: metrics"
            print "      - action: pprof"
            print ""
            skip = 1; done = 1; next
        }
        skip && /^(# HTTP-based|[a-zA-Z])/ { skip = 0 }
        skip { next }
        /^rtspTransports:/ { print "rtspTransports: [tcp]"; next }
        { print }
        END { if (!done) exit 1 }
    ' "$tmp/mediamtx.yml" > "$tmp/mediamtx.new" || fail "MediaMTX's default config has changed, so the install can't lock publishing. Choose an earlier version."
    mv -f "$tmp/mediamtx.new" mediamtx.yml
    echo "Publishing needs the user publish with the password $password (change it in mediamtx.yml)."
fi
echo "Installed MediaMTX $version."

variables.name: Version
variables.description: The MediaMTX version to install, such as 1.21.4, or latest.

variables.name: RTMP port
variables.description: The port OBS and other RTMP software publish to and read from. Add it to the server's ports first.

variables.name: HLS port
variables.description: The web port that serves streams to browsers over HLS. Add it to the server's ports first.

variables.name: WebRTC port
variables.description: The web port for WebRTC viewers and publishers (TCP). Add it to the server's ports first.

variables.name: WebRTC media port
variables.description: The UDP port WebRTC sends media over. Add it to the server's ports first.

variables.name: SRT port
variables.description: The UDP port for SRT publishers and readers. Add it to the server's ports first.
